claims.text: TypeSafe AI opened early access to Jev, their SystemOne model, in the week before this post (September 2026).
GeoDeploy compares every AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud region that offers managed Kubernetes and provisions Kubernetes across all three providers.
TypeSafe's Jev provides AI primitives that let apps, agents, and workflows make decisions based on context.
Jev's decision-making primitives are confidence scoring, multiple choice, and yes/no (noul) questions.
Jev's decision-making primitives are the perfect complement to agentic work.
GeoDeploy fetches current prices from the AWS Price List API, the Azure Retail Prices API, and the Google Cloud Billing Catalog.
GeoDeploy composes Pulumi programs from typed modules: EKS, AKS, GKE; ECR, ACR, Artifact Registry; DNS through Route 53, NS1, or Cloudflare.
The Pulumi Automation API runs a preview then an update with one stack per region, and GeoDeploy won't run unless cloud credentials pass readiness checks.
Every GeoDeploy run writes plan.json and plan.md with the full decision record.
Jev's choice() returns the pick, a probability distribution across options, and a confidence; score() rates against a rubric; noul() answers a yes/no question with a single probability.
GeoDeploy's score() rubrics use 10 levels.
GeoDeploy sends Jev a shortlist of up to 40 priced candidates per geo.
GeoDeploy asks Jev in a single call for one selection, five quality scores, two hard checks, and a fallback.
The Jev SDK package is @typesafe-ai/sdk exporting choice, noul, and score.
TypeSafe's advice for rubrics is to 'describe situations, not degrees.'
The TypeSafe SDK exposes TypeSafeClient with a systemOne method taking state and questions and returning answers.
GeoDeploy weight profiles are latency-optimized (default), balanced, residency-first, and failure-domain with the listed weights.
GeoDeploy confidence thresholds: residency 0.95 hard reject; new cluster region 0.90; existing stack region 0.75; ingress/autoscaling 0.85; node-pool sizing 0.60; global floor 0.50.
Jev only selects from closed sets, so a hallucinated region or made-up Pulumi argument can't happen by construction.
On gate failure, API timeout/error, or unreachable upstream, GeoDeploy falls back to deterministic price comparison enforcing residency and constraints; `geodeploy explain` shows why each region won.
In self-driving mode (`geodeploy monitor`), above 0.85 confidence resize is applied automatically, 0.70–0.85 is suggested for human approval, below 0.70 falls back to a deterministic rule.
CPU utilization alone is a poor autoscaling metric and is usually paired with other signals.
GeoDeploy is open source at github.com/pulumi/devx-geodeploy.
The link /automation/ points to the Pulumi Automation API page.
